data.short_meaning: Given to the one who is given
data.long_meaning: The name Khateemah is derived from the Arabic root 'khtm' which means 'to give'. It is the name given to the one who is given, bestowed, or honored. In Islamic history, Khateemah is the name of a noblewoman who was the wife of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham). The name Khateemah carries the meaning “Given to the one who is given” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khateemah usually hope their child will grow to embody given to the one who is given and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Khateemah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Given to the one who is given.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khateemah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مؤنث يعني النهاية أو الختام، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة آل عمران الآية ١٤٤، خاتمة للكلام أو العمل، ويدل على الاكتمال والتمام. وفي الاصطلاح، يطلق على آخر النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم خاتم النبين، وعلى آخر الكتب السماوية القرآن الكريم خاتمة الكتب.

in_english.name: Khateemah
in_english.long_meaning: Khateemah is a feminine given name derived from the Arabic root خ-ت-م (kha-ta-ma), meaning 'to seal' or 'to conclude'. In Islamic tradition, the name Khateemah signifies the final or last, often referring to the Prophet Muhammad as 'Khatam al-Anbiya' (Seal of the Prophets) and the Quran as the final revelation. The name embodies completeness, finality, and perfection.
